key_insight: TerraZero shows that a fast procedural simulator plus zero-demonstration self-play can train autonomous driving policies that generalize across cities, traffic rules, and long-tail scenarios.
engineering_relevance: The system combines CPU simulation and GPU inference in a zero-copy architecture to reach 1.3M agent-steps per second, making large-scale RL for driving practical on a single server-grade GPU.
method: Procedurally rebuilds scenarios from logged map geometry while randomizing road users, signals, dynamics, rewards, and vehicle sizes each episode.
Uses a configurable C engine for simulation and self-play RL training with no human demonstrations and no fallback planner at inference.
Supports heterogeneous agents and multiple dynamics models, including cars, trucks, pedestrians, and cyclists.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports zero-shot generalization across cities and datasets, emergent left-hand-traffic behavior, top performance on the InterPlan long-tail benchmark, strong results on val14, and competitive realism on Waymo Open Sim Agents.
watch_item: Because the simulator is procedurally grounded in map geometry and rule-based agents, performance may depend on how well the randomized rules and dynamics cover real-world edge cases.
paper_title: TerraZero: Procedural Driving Simulation for Zero-Demonstration Self-Play at Scale
